speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. I see you have a painful, ulcerative skin lesion on your leg; to begin our evaluation, how long has this lesion been present, and has it changed in appearance or size?

speaker: Patient
text: 54-year-old woman. The patient reports a skin lesion on her right leg that has been present for 1 month. The lesion began as a small red spot and has increased in size. She recalls an ant bite at the site before the lesion developed. She has a history of anterior uveitis treated with corticosteroids 8 months ago, as well as Crohn's disease, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and hypertension.

speaker: Doctor
text: Based on your history of Crohn's disease, diabetes, and recent steroid use, combined with the lesion growing over a month following an "ant bite," I need to clarify the lesion's characteristics. Is it warm or draining, and does it have raised, rolled edges? REQUEST TEST: Complete Blood Count (CBC) and C-Reactive Protein (CRP).

speaker: Patient
text:
My main symptom is Painful ulcerative lesion on the right leg. I also have Lesion has a central necrotic base and purplish irregular borders, History of ant bite at the site of the lesion, Pitting pedal edema of the lower extremities, Dilated tortuous veins in both lower legs.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Pyoderma Gangrenosum (likely pathergy-induced by the reported "ant bite").

The description of a painful ulcer with a central necrotic base, purplish irregular borders, and the patient's history of Crohn's disease and recent steroid use is highly characteristic of Pyoderma Gangrenosum. The "ant bite" was likely a traumatic event (pathergy) that triggered the lesion at this site, which is distinct from a simple cellulitis or spider bite.
